Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
228 PM EDT Wed Sep 2 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
A Severe Thunderstorm Watch is in effect until 5pm for Maryland
from Allegany County to Cecil County to St. Mary's County and
for eastern portions of West Virginia and much of northeastern
and central Virginia. Within the next hour, we may be canceling
the northern half of our watch as convection has weakened and 
moved out to the south.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Daily severe weather threat through the end of the week.

- 2) Hot and humid conditions yield likely record high minimum 
     temperatures this week.

- 3) Heat & thunderstorms begin to decrease heading into 
     Labor Day weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Daily severe weather threat through the end of 
the week.

The original Mesoscale Convective Complex that moved out of
Pennsylvania into our CWA late this morning has now bowed well 
south and east out over the Delmarva and central Chesapeake 
Bay and is aligned to the west and northwest into northeastern
Virginia and northwest into eastern West Virginia. Winds have
gusted between 45 to 65 mph within this complex, while isolated
supercell thunderstorms that have become severe from Hampshire
County to Fauquier County are producing large hail with damaging
winds. Round two of thunderstorm clusters could develop
somewhere over western or northwest Pennsylvania later this
afternoon before racing east and southeast again toward our
area. Confidence in timing and initiation of such thunderstorms
are uncertain. We almost need to wait until storms start
developing then we can track it and time better. This particular
setup of transferring from Round 1 to Round 2 may be similar
should be get Round 3 or 4 overnight tonight through Thursday
night. By Friday, cold front should clear much of the forecast 
area causing a stabilizing effect limiting the risk of severe 
weather, but showers and thunderstorms will still be possible 
north of the sfc front. Timing seems to slow with later model
runs of this outcome. 


KEY MESSAGE 2...Hot and humid conditions yield likely record 
high minimum temperatures this week.

Decent model agreement that areas south of US-33 and US-211 will
see heat indices meet heat advisory criteria this afternoon.
Based on yesterday's high temperature readings and greater
confidence, issued Heat Advisories for the southern half of the
fcst area. 

Thursday's max temperature forecast has a lot more 
uncertainty due to potential for more convection. If convection
doesn't materialize, more record high minimums are possible
again today, but that doesn't seem likely at this time, except
only at Charlottesville. 

Record high minimum temperatures were set yesterday at IAD, DCA,
and HGR. RERs were issued earlier. 


KEY MESSAGE 3...Heat & thunderstorms begin to decrease heading into 
Labor Day weekend.

High pressure tracks southeast from the Great Lakes on Saturday, 
pushing a cold front through region throughout the day. Some 
uncertainty still exists regarding how far south this front 
will advance south before stalling, but most ensemble members 
depict this boundary south of our region by Saturday afternoon. 
This should bring a drop in heat & humidity across the Mid-
Atlantic, with afternoon highs ranging in the mid-80s on 
Saturday. As mid-level dry air continues to track across the 
area, temperatures should continue to decrease as the weekened 
goes on. By the Labor Day holiday, it should feel relatively 
mild & dry, with dewpoints ranging in the upper-50s across the 
region. 

&&

.AVIATION /18Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
Multiple rounds of thunderstorms this afternoon through Friday.
Given low confidence on timing, issued PROB30 groups for now. As
thunderstorms develop and show signs of motion, then we can go
to Tempo groups or certain from groups.

This weekend, prevailing VFR conditions are expected across all 
terminals. A few showers and thunderstorms Saturday afternoon & 
evening could reduce flight categories briefly near the KCHO 
terminal. Light northwesterly winds on Saturday shift to 
easterly and calm by Sunday evening. 

&&

.MARINE...
Winds 10kt or less outside of thunderstorms. SMWs likely through
the early evening and then again overnight into Thursday again.

On Friday and Saturday, winds below 15kts most of the time, but 
higher winds and waves could during afternoon and evening showers or 
thunderstorms. light northwesterly winds shift easterly by Saturday 
afternoon.

&&

.CLIMATE...
Record high minimums were set yesterday at IAD, DCA, and HGR.
Please RERs for detail info. More record high minimums are
possible again tonight and Thursday night.
